name: Nations & the believer
about: God's judgment on nations, and the believer in them.

teachings.title: Nations blessed or bred out by God
teachings.summary: God judges physical nations, and whether that judgment slows depends not on the unsaved but on saved Christians, chiefly by winning souls.
teachings.text:
There's a pernicious Jew myth popular among some on the right, is sold to the ignorant and the unsaved, and that is that Christianity has no room in it for nationalism. That is a universalist belief system. That's only in matters of salvation.

Physical Nations on Earth of common people who live God-fearing lives are blessed and thrive, and those that fall away are bred out of existence. That's the judgment of God.

The Bible says that if you want that judgment to reverse or slow down even a little, it doesn't depend on what the degenerate unsaved people do, it depends on what the saved Bible believing Christians do. And the primary thing is winning souls to Christ.

teachings.title: Make us a king like all the nations
teachings.summary: Like Israel demanding a king, Americans seek political overthrow, but every system is judged by God when it turns from Him, so the answer is getting people right with God.
teachings.text:
**1 Samuel 8:5**

*And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.*

This is the spirit far too many Americans find themselves in today, wanting to overthrow the current system entirely because it's leaders are corrupt and the people are wicked.

Even the Israelites, with the perfect system of God being their King, the law literally set in stone, and Godly men given power by God to judge them, still went through cycles where they failed the system, and were captured or occupied. Where their own wicked deeds brought about decades of oppression, and it's only by turning to the Lord and repenting of that evil do we see them return to prosperity.

It doesn't matter if we are a monarchy, democracy, fascist, socialist, a dictatorship... We are going to be judged by God if we turn away from Him.

That's why all of this debate about political solutions to our spiritual problem is vain and foolish. Work on getting enough people right with God and the rest will sort itself.

teachings.title: Turning toward the Lord is all we have
teachings.summary: Only Bible-believing Christians turning from their own wicked ways to God can delay the wrath America deserves; voting, shooting or vengeance are vanity.
teachings.text:
It is in the hands of Christians, Bible believing, born again sons of God, to turn away from their wicked ways, their indulgence in the world, in sin, in the subversive and perverse things we are tempted with, and turn towards God the Father, in Jesus' name.

All other methods of delaying the wrath that America deserves are vanity. We cannot vote our way out. We cannot shoot our way out. We cannot riot and murder and exact our own vengeance, and expect any relief.

There is only one path. Turning to the right or left leads to destruction. Turning towards the Lord is all we have. #IndependenceDay #4thofJuly

teachings.title: If my people which are called by my name
teachings.summary: Nations are judged by the works of those who call themselves by God's name, and the promise of 2 Chronicles 7:14 extends to every nation with Christians in it.
teachings.text:
The judgment of nations is by their works, and more, the fruit of those among them that call themselves by His name.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land*.

This promise is extended to every nation, that has Christians living in it. And every nation on earth has saved Christians among them. Or those apostates calling themselves by His name, yet chasing idols and drunk on the fornications of their mother church.

As we watch the inevitable destruction of our nation coming, as Jeremiah did in visions from the Lord, we can relate to him, and how he felt. Yet take comfort in the fact that even in his Lamentations, he held fast to the hope of the promise of the Lord.

teachings.title: Ye are the salt of the earth
teachings.summary: People are saved by faith alone, but nations are judged by Christians' works, so America's decline comes from believers losing their savour and not turning from wickedness, which is not persecution for righteousness' sake.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalm 37**, God promises that the wicked shall be cut down like grass, while those that trust in the Lord and do good shall dwell in the land and be fed.

This is a crucial detail in the Christian life, and the fate of our families and nation. The conditional understanding, that those who trust in the Lord, His people, the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus, are given the opportunity to have life, in abundance, though obedience to the commandments of God. To do good.

We are given eternal life by faith in Christ Jesus alone. Trusting God. But our lives on this earth are judged by the good that we do.

People are judged by faith. Nations are judged by Christians' works.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

It is a popular verse, quoted often from pulpits across America. And it shows that there is a solution to the chaos and depravity affecting our society, and that solution is not found in consuming political commentary or voting. It is turning towards God and away from evil, as His people.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.*

Salt is a preservative that keeps meat from spoiling. It not only stops the rotting, but improves the flavor and texture of it when cooked. When tried by the fire.

We are to be that salt, and when the Christian loses his savour, we see that we become useless, and are left to be trodden down, and rightfully so.

This is in contrast with the earlier verse;

**Matthew 5:10–12**
*Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.*

We often hear Christians complain about being vexed by the filthy conversation of the wicked, and who treat the inevitable trodding down caused by our lack of commitment and separation, as persecution for righteousness sake. They are not the same.

In fact, many Christians live as the world, not doing good that they may dwell in the land, and act surprised when the wicked prosper and our nation is flooded with strangers, bringing their idolatry and paganism with them.

They act as though they are being persecuted by politicians and corrupt leaders, while in reality we are the cause.

We become fearful and resentful, fretting about evildoers and being envious of the workers of iniquity.

We ignore God's prescriptions for what ails us, and so we forsake the promises of safety and provision He has given us.

teachings.title: Romans 13: obey until the law is explicitly anti-Christ
teachings.summary: Those who reject the plain reading of Romans 13 often harbour wrath, and believers should pay tribute and live without offence until the law openly demands they deny God, then obey God and accept persecution.
teachings.text:
I find people not amenable to the literal reading of Romans 13:1-7 are despising government because they are harboring sinful, wrathful thoughts and don't want to believe that puts them directly on the path of "*if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God.*"

Or maybe they know, and want to escape the sword. Or maybe they are afraid of the implied persecution. Maybe they fear it becoming actual.

Because as long as there is an *implied* anti-White, anti-Christian persecution behind most govt/system policies, there is fear and reactionary incidents (primed by fake ones) with a million reprobate psychopaths MKUltraed from birth, but no change. It's a stalemate.

The point is when it comes to those matters that may turn hypothetical into reality, like supporting biblical doctrine on sodomites and adulterers, for example, or understanding that Jews are antichrists, by definition, bodily autonomy as a temple of the Holy Spirit, etc, in faith, without fear, and accepting that you may be persecuted for His sake, we must answer to the higher power, which is God.

Until then, we live of no offense. Paying tribute. Paying custom. Not breaking the law, until the law is explicitly anti-Christ.

Make them say it.

Make them say you're salvation is hate and they want to shut it down.

teachings.title: Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers
teachings.summary: God ordains the powers that be, even wicked rulers, so revolting against them is sin, and liberty comes from Christ rather than from a worship of freedom itself.
teachings.text:
And so;

*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

God puts the people in power over us, to His purpose. Even the wicked.

*Whosoever therefore resisteth the power, resisteth the ordinance of God: and they that resist shall receive to themselves damnation.*

Damnation in this sense for the saved is physical, but in the broader sense it is a sin to revolt against things that aren't contradicted by the higher power, the highest being God.

*For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to the evil. Wilt thou then not be afraid of the power? do that which is good, and thou shalt have praise of the same:*

Think of Daniel, given us for an example. He never compromised what was right, but did well in that framework that even under evil powers, he prospered.

*For he is the minister of God to thee for good. But if thou do that which is evil, be afraid; for he beareth not the sword in vain: for he is the minister of God, a revenger to execute wrath upon him that doeth evil. Wherefore ye must needs be subject, not only for wrath, but also for conscience sake.*

ACAB. FAAFO. Molon labe. Don't tread on me. The twisting of our liberty in Christ and the blessings that follow, into a cult of individuality that worships Liberty itself as a god leads to entitlement, pride, justification for wickedness and an abandonment of fear of God, and an adoption of fear of EVERYTHING that may infringe on our "freedoms."

But we know, the meek shall inherit the earth. We know that we, as peacemakers are blessed. That as much as possible if it be within us, we should live peaceably with all men.

Jews, who are in open rebellion against God, who killed the prophets and Christ Jesus, are contrary to all men and God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost.

The shift from understanding liberty comes from faith through Christ by grace, to it being something we deserve in itself, is a Jewish trick.

Tocqueville, the Frenchman who toured early America concluded that the preservation of America’s traditional religion, the Puritan and Baptist faith in Christ, and the understanding that our liberty is from sin, through Him, is one of the most important tasks of democratic statesmanship. He wrote that religion “should be considered the first” of America’s “political institutions” and even that it is necessary for Americans to “maintain Christianity…at all cost.”

But God judges nations based on how the people who call themselves by His name, act.

So when we as a nation, White Heritage Americans, Christians, abandoned the faith and our our own libertine rights over the blessings of liberty in Christ, the ministers appointed by God, who hold the sword not in vain, turn against us.

But God made a promise of salvation for nations too.

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: Those offended by Romans 13 do not do the work
teachings.summary: Those who call for insurrection instead of obeying Romans 13 show a lack of faith and neglect the real work God asks: the word, church, prayer and winning souls.
teachings.text:
When I hear the fearful and angry calling for insurrection, I see their lack of faith. They don't walk in the spirit and so they fulfill the lusts of the flesh. And they get what they deserve.

And of this sin, I am chief. I have and am subject to the same outrage and fears, when I don't walk after the spirit.

I have lost friends, who professed Christ and said the things we expect a saved person to confess, who became offended by the idea that they are the cause for our misfortune. That if they had faith they wouldn't be afraid, and not being afraid, able to protect their families and community, blessed by God.

They call that weak. They say if God doesn't want us to just sit around and let Him do all the work. They claim God expects us to stand up ourselves.

And this is true.

God asks us to read and study His word. To go to church and work towards edifying it. To preach the Gospel to every creature. To be instant in prayer. To help the brokenhearted, to give hope to the hopeless. To win souls.

And, to a man, those that are offended by Romans 13, who are insisting we "do something!" Do none of those things.

They may join a church or denomination, seeking an identity. A trad and based label to join, to further their politics. But they don't actually walk as a Christian. They may even recruit others to their denomination, but it's because they are seeking power, not out of compassion to save souls.

Know the signs, examine yourselves. See it in others and make a difference that they turn to God, giving Him His wrath and Vengeance, not taking it themselves.

teachings.title: Render tribute: not paying taxes is sin
teachings.summary: Under Romans 13 refusing to pay taxes or obey the law on them is sin, and pastors who teach it are as harmful as false prophets.
teachings.text:
*For for this cause pay ye tribute also: for they are God's ministers, attending continually upon this very thing. Render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom; fear to whom fear; honour to whom honour.*

Not paying taxes and breaking the law regarding how they are administered, even to a church, is a sin.

You can pray they be lowered. You can be thankful God has made your church exempt. You can even take advantage of the various ways to structure your finances or your church's finances in a way that best serves to maintain the Spirit of the law and service to the Gospel.

But a so-called pastor in a living room church, refusing to obey the law and encouraging others to do the same almost always is a false prophet and as damaging to the cause of Christ as a false prophet who abuses the system to create a 501c3 in order to mislead people, too.

They are the same.

teachings.title: Josiah removed the sodomites
teachings.summary: Good kings like Josiah tore down idols and removed the sodomites to win reprieve for the nation, so Christians must stand firmly against sodomites and evil.
teachings.text:
**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*if my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

We see throughout the Old Testament that the people of Israel, given every advantage by the blessings of God, His protection, the law, the ordinances, the faith in the Christ to come delivered by the Spirit unto the prophets, and yet they continually turn to Idolatry, building altars and groves, burning incense to the hosts of heaven, bowing down before strange gods, passing their children through the fire; killing them as a sacrifice to Baal, and tolerating the houses of the sodomites which do the abominations of the nations God has driven out of the promised land.

And God's wrath was kindled against the people. And He swore destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel and Judah.

But good kings came occasionally, and did what was right in the sight of the Lord, and when they did, they bought their people reprieve, as God repented for a time of the evil He was to do.

The Bible is clear in these accounts that not only did they tear down altars and kill the priests worshipping idols and burning incense to false gods (ahem RCC), but the sodomites were killed and removed from the land.

As we enter into June, it is important that we who call ourselves by His name, Christians, stand firmly opposed to the sodomites and all those who defy the judgment of God.

Like Josiah, who when he read the book of the law found in the Temple, rent his clothes and called for revival, being moved by the word of God, we must do the same. In season or out of season. Even if we are persecuted and attacked for it. We must call our evil when it is presented to us and have no fellowship with the sons of Belial.

teachings.title: Benjamin protected the sodomites
teachings.summary: Judges 19-21 shows God commanding war on Benjamin for protecting sodomites, a picture of our days when every man does what is right in his own eyes.
teachings.text:
The book of Judges is a difficult one, detailing the history between the settling of Israel under Joshua, and before the era of kings that begins with Saul. There are great heroes in the book, like Gideon and Sampson, but the key lesson throughout is that not everyone in the Bible behaves righteously. Many are wicked and sinful. The key to understanding is found in the often-repeated verse; *In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.*

That's the larger context. That even when the people turn to the Lord and do the right thing, it isn't always for the right reasons and many times they just do what they think is right in their own eyes.

All this to say the story told in Judges 19-21, of the sodomites protected within the tribe of Benjamin, and God's command to smite the tribe, He giving the others of Israel victory over them for their condoning and protecting these wicked sons of Belial, is very illustrative of the times we live in today, where people do what is right in their own eyes. Regardless of anything else; people were rightfully shocked and disgusted by the actions of the sodomites, and the willingness of Benjamin to fight to the death to protect those abominations. The fracture this war against a fellow tribe caused many divisions as we see. Much death. But the sodomites and most of their protectors were removed from the land.

teachings.title: The evil of sodomites given free reign
teachings.summary: The Gibeah outrage parallels Sodom to show the evil of a nation allowing sodomites free reign, which God's law calls an abomination worthy of death.
teachings.text:
*And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel*...and we know, men did what was right in their own eyes.

**Judges 19** begins another tale of the excesses and depravity that Israel fell into absent a Moses or Joshua. Relying on regional judges to come forth by God to deliver them from the results that came from the abominations they fell into.

This channel has covered the story told in **Judges 19-21** before, because it deals directly with the evil of allowing sodomites free reign in a nation.

The parallel to **Genesis 19** and the story of the destruction of Sodom is meant to drive home the point. Parallelism is God's way of signifying the importance of the message He is conveying.

A mob of baser fellows of the lewd sort, sons of Belial, Sodomites, surround a house in a city they are allowed free reign in, and there demand the master of the house deliver up a stranger, a man, that they may know him. These dogs burn with lust one for another, working that which is unseemly. Men with men, laying together. Abominations.

Worse they seek to force it by violence, in a mob. To a stranger, a sojourner. A Levite, of the priesthood.

None of the law or the things of God mattered to these reprobates, not retaining Him in their minds. Their conscience seared with a hot iron. Being twice-dead, fit to be burned.

**Leviticus 18:22**
*Thou shalt not lie with mankind, as with womankind: it is abomination.*

**Leviticus 20:13**
*If a man also lie with mankind, as he lieth with a woman, both of them have committed an abomination: they shall surely be put to death; their blood shall be upon them.*

**Deuteronomy 23:17**
*There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.*

**Romans 1:29-32**
*being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers, backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents, without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful: who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.*

teachings.title: Evolution undermines the case for nations
teachings.theme: God sets the bounds of nations
teachings.summary: Evolution's change-or-die logic justifies race mixing and erasing borders, whereas nations exist and are blessed or destroyed by God's handiwork and judgment.
teachings.text:
Rather than provide a basis and rationalizations for race and ethnicity, and justification for segregation and nations, the theory of evolution actually undermines all of it with its central tenant of 'change or die.'

If evolution is real, and all creatures when exposed to other forces must change over time, seeking genetic dominance and continuation, then how is it not only natural but advantageous for the mixing of races, the dominance of the sub-Saharan population as it spreads across Europe, for example. Or the American erasure of Anglo-Germanic stock, replaced by brown goblins?

How can one make an argument for national purity for what is currently an endangered species in the face of overwhelming pressures to adapt and change? To cross breed for advantage? To erase borders as outdated constructs, giving way instead to migratory patterns of a global natural selection?

It is with the God of the Bible and His handiwork that we have nations of men. It is His judgement that blesses and destroys bloodlines, ethnicities, nations.

It may feel easier to blame it all on the vagaries of chance, the fickle forces of evolution changing man over time, and place hope on some sort of eugenic natural preservation system, like we have for elephants or panda bears, to keep Whites as a race, alive. Easier than turning to God and allowing Him to heal your nation and keep it and bless it. But in the long run you simply shoot your own cause in the foot.

teachings.title: No moral case for nations without a Creator
teachings.theme: God sets the bounds of nations
teachings.summary: Without a purposeful Creator who set nations and their habitations there is no moral case for preserving a people, as natural selection does not care.
teachings.text:
Consider the Nation of Britain, which has gone from a global empire of dominance, to being completely subsumed by foreign phenotypes to the point of extinction, all within a few generations. A blink of time, if you believe that billions and billions of years were your creator, rather than the God of the Bible.

How is that not simply a natural evolution, even desirous, if weaker adaptations, ill suited for their changing environment, are meant to die out? For stronger, or at least better suited genetics to rise in status and pass on its genetic advantage?

What moral case for preservation of an ethnicity, a race of people, a nation? Their boundaries and habitations? What moral case can be made absent a purposeful creator who gave us these things?

The godless and purposeful process of natural selection provides no moral or even intellectual mooring in that debate. Securing a future for your children isn't something that matters to the god of evolution.

It simply doesn't care.

teachings.title: Babel: God scattered them into nations
teachings.theme: God sets the bounds of nations
teachings.summary: At Babel God confounded one-world man-made unity and scattered men into nations by kindred, and the genealogies mark the time from Adam to Christ.
teachings.text:
*And the whole earth was of one language, and the Lord said, Behold the people is one, and they have all one language...now nothing will be restrained of them, which they imagine to do.*

100 years after the flood, in the year of Pelig's birth (*for in his days was the earth divided*), the people imagined a vain thing. A tower to Heaven.

That they could work their way to Heaven and be like God.

*Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another's speech*.

LORD God, the Father says "*let us go down*..."

And they scattered the people and confused their language. We are meant to be in nations. Nations by clan. By blood. Not one world government, full of vanity. Not even by a civic nationalism of paper and statutes that erases who we are, *making a name for ourselves lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.*

Nimrod gets a bad rap, having founded Babel and being a mighty man, a hunter before the LORD, it is assumed he's the impetus for the construction of the tower. Most of the assumption is based on his proximity, greatness, being a *gibboram* or mighty man, and his lineage forming the great cities listed in Genesis 10, Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

Some translate his name as "deserter," others "he rebelled" and take this to build an entire story around him, the tower, and great wickedness against God. Yet scripture doesn't give a negative accounting of him.

And then we are given the generations of Shem, leading to Terah father of Abraham and uncle to Lot.

And thus the genealogy of man after the flood is again given to establish where and when we are for the next phase of the story being told; the origins and chronology of the people whom God dealt with. Adam to Noah. Noah to Abram. And in like manner, the Gospels have similar genealogies, bringing us to Jesus Christ, that we have a lineage and time frame from Adam to Jesus earthly incarnation.

Many over look this as simply a history or chronological device, and try to extract much deeper meaning from it than is there, and often at the expense of believing it literally, especially the timing of years.

Also note, that the life spans of man are shrinking as we go from Shem to Abram. Approaching the 120yr avg God decided back in Genesis 6. Abraham would be 170 when he died. A shadow of the 900yrs most of the earlier patriarchs lived to.

teachings.title: Restitution, not prisons: God's just law
teachings.summary: God's law of restitution for theft is just and perfect, and a nation living by His judgments would be better than man's criminal justice system.
teachings.text:
As we continue through the ordinances for the Levitical priesthood and sacrifices, we are also given more insight into the law, building on the fundamental of loving thy neighbor.

The sin of robbery by guile or by violence, by any dishonest means, was punished by restitution plus 5%, and a trespass offering. That's it.

Now as we saw yesterday, this required a confession of the wrong in order to share in the sacrifice for atonement, and obviously to restore the person who suffered loss.

God says this is just.

Man says we must create an entire criminal justice system with prisons and punishment, cops and robbers.

As we saw in Exodus 21, 22, there are more provisions for theft, and include instructions for those impenitent to or destitute to be given to servitude to repay. If they are caught breaking in and killed by the owner, there is no blood guilt. If there is harm done. Eye for an eye. Tooth for a tooth. Stripe for stripe.

God's law is perfect. It may not be able to save us, sinners as we all are. But for a nation to live by His perfect judgments, if they were to be followed, it would be a much better country. In our founding, much of the original laws came from the Old Testament. They are right and just.

**1 Timothy 1:8-11**
*But we know that the law is good, if a man use it lawfully; knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, for whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; according to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

teachings.title: God's civil law still judges nations
teachings.summary: The civil punishments of Leviticus 20, unlike the ceremonial ordinances, are God's standard for judging nations and remain in effect today.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 20** begins laying out specific punishments for the violations of the civil laws given to Moses and Aaron by God, especially the paganism and the sexual immorality listed in the previous chapters. The sins of those whose lands the children of Israel were entering into, and the land the Lord freed them from, Egypt.

And as God frequently has stated in giving this law, the purpose was to separate the people unto God and away from the error, whoredoms and abominations of the other nations. To be holy because He is holy.

The law of God is perfect. His judgments are righteous. A just nation seeking after the Lord, who have the fear of God, would implement these strictures and punishments, that their nation not be judged, and the land that the Lord has granted them the habitations thereof wouldn't spew them out.

And so, as a practical matter, these things given by God, not to be confused with the ordinances and sacrifices that were done away with in the reformation of Christ, but rather are His law by which He judges nations. They are in full effect, even today. And His wrath is clearly upon those nations that don't follow His precepts.

teachings.title: Cut off for Molech and familiar spirits
teachings.summary: God commanded that those who gave children to Molech or went after mediums be cut off, showing His perfect will for a people seeking to be holy.
teachings.text:
And so, practically, physically, these laws give us insight to the perfect will of God for a people.

We start with a continuation of the following after false gods from chapter 19, where if a man offers his seed, that is his children, to Moloch, the false god of the Canaanites, he shall be cut off. Not allowed to defile the house of the Lord. Stoned to death, God's face turned from him. Reprobation. He is rejected and it is up to the people to do as God commanded and not to ignore his presence among them. This rejection is both physical and spiritual,  (I want to focus on the literal application as we go through the list of sins and punishment, tying in the spiritual application afterwards.)

Next he warns against those who go after mediums; those who have "familiar spirits," and after wizards, they too shall be cut off, the mediums and wizards stoned to death. Note these things are closely aligned with the false gods, because they are not only satanic but mean the person has no respect for the Lord, no fear of the living God, and has no faith in Him that saves, but rather seeks another god of their own invention. Reprobate concerning the faith, and physically cut off from the nation seeking to be holy. Sanctified.

*Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you.*

Again, separation by keeping God's statutes, that He may sanctify us. Something that Israel failed to do, and were cut off for when, after the longsuffering of God was over, Jesus had come in the flesh.

teachings.title: Abortion: passing children through the fire
teachings.summary: Abortion is today's child sacrifice to Molech and Mammon, and the women burdened by it should be reached with the gospel before their hearts are hardened.
teachings.text:
*And thou shalt not let any of thy seed pass through the fire to Molech, neither shalt thou profane the name of thy God: I am the Lord*.

Sacrifice of children to false gods was a common practice in every age and nation. We know that today, it is done through abortion. In Canaan, they sacrificed to Moloch. Today, it is often Mammon. It is horribly wicked. The bloody sacrifices to devils of their own children leads many to reprobation.

Women today have been pressured with unrelenting propaganda and social and economic incentives to use abortifacients as "birth control" and infanticide, while men have abandoned their proper role as a husband and father. Many, especially the women, carry this burden of sin and pain and are brokenhearted from it. It is important to try and reach them with the Gospel before they harden their hearts to sear their conscience.

teachings.title: Nations judged for shedding innocent blood
teachings.summary: A nation that refuses to punish those who shed innocent blood, whether by repealing capital punishment, funding abortion or bombing innocents, is guilty of that blood and God will judge it, so believers must stand against it.
teachings.text:
**Deuteronomy 21** ramps up the commands of God in this, Moses giving of the law prior to entering the promised land. The land given as an inheritance to the children of Israel, if they maintain these rules to keep it. And right away God has let them know that the abominations of the Canaanites, their worship of idols and the shedding of innocent blood, were the cause of their own destruction. God judges nations for these things.

Here specifically, God gives provision for an unsolved murder along the wayside or in the wilderness. If a body be found, slain, and the elders of the nearest city do not know who did it, they were to take a heifer and offer a sacrifice, washing their hands of the matter. This of course is an image of Christ, as all the sacrifices pictured, the washing of the hands to show innocence before God for the bloodshed is just as Pontius Pilate did.

As the Lord declared to Noah; *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.*

**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren.*

**Psalms 11:5**
*The LORD trieth the righteous: but the wicked and him that loveth violence his soul hateth.*

When a nation has refused to slay those who shed innocent blood, they are guilty of it. And God will repay. Be it repealing capital punishment, refusing to sentence a murderer to death, justifying or even funding abortions, bombing Innocents abroad, all these things bring judgment on a people, and the land will spew them out.

**Leviticus 18:28**
*That the land spew not you out also, when ye defile it, as it spewed out the nations that were before you.*

God requires of us that we stand against the shedding of innocent blood and seek His justice against those that do it.

teachings.title: If my people shall humble themselves
teachings.summary: A nation is saved by its believers turning to God, as promised in 2 Chronicles 7:14, not by online poses and ideological debates.
teachings.text:
Honestly, if you all dropped the stupid pose for like 5 seconds, we could accomplish so much legitimately, and in faith.

But you're also worked up about every current thing, or engaging in "who would win in a fight.." ideological debates that go nowhere, that you've lost sight of the big picture.

Live worthy of a Godly nation, and remember that God's wrath is in His time. But the biggest delay is having a people worth saving because they turned to the Lord. That's on you. That's on me.

It is saved believers turning towards God that saves a nation.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

That's a promise.

But so few believe the report....

teachings.title: Revival starts with the children of light
teachings.summary: A nation slouching toward Gomorrah fails because Christians compromise, so revival begins with believers walking in the Spirit, honest and submitted to God.
teachings.text:
So, again, the question of why we as a nation (because God judges nations here on earth), ...why as a nation are we failing, slouching to Gomorrah?

Is it the children of darkness, of wrath? Doing the unseemly things they do, not having the light within? As they flail around in the darkness?

Or is it the people who call themselves by His name, going along with it? The children of the light? Not shining the light but walking after the ways of the unsaved and unbelieving? Compromising, and so being compromised...

It starts with us. We lead revival. Not with flowery words and enabling our own sin. Not with judgment designed to puff us up, and rationalize our faults as, "at least, not as bad as those sinners over there."

We do it by walking in the Spirit. We do that by staying in the word, in prayer, in praise and thanksgiving. By being honest in our dealings. In meekly having a ready answer to our hope, which isn't in our works and good deeds, such as they are, but in Christ. By submitting to God, and His will for us. To honor our roles.

This is what brings blessings to a nation, when the people who call themselves Christian act like it, and in doing so bring others into the same light.

teachings.title: God's if/then covenants with nations
teachings.summary: God's covenants with nations are conditional, judging nations by their works while He judges individuals by faith, and a nation that turns from wickedness can still be healed.
teachings.text:
We see near the end, after the triumphant singing and dancing unto the Lord, that the Isralites first begin to complain. And God makes a covenant with them as a nation, through Moses.

 *If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.*

All of God's covenants with the Hebrew are if/then. All come with responsibility of the people to hold to what God asks. This is the covenants with nations. With the people on this earth. God judges us as individuals spiritually by faith, but God judges nations on earth by their works.

This invitation to nations is still around today. It is how a godly nation that turns from its wicked ways becomes spared the evil God will do unto it.

*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: The wine cup of God's fury on all nations
teachings.summary: God judges nations by their works while saving individuals by faith, and His fury poured on Judah and its neighbours foreshadows the judgment on end-times Babylon.
teachings.text:
In **Jeremiah 25** we see that the prophet has been preaching the word of God for 23 years, and he was not alone. Zephaniah and Habakkuk, and eventually Daniel and Ezekiel (after captivity began), are Jeremiah's contemporaries. The prophets of God trying to make strait the paths of Judah, while God uses His "servant," Babylon as the rod to lead them back to Him.

In chapter 25 we see the preaching of destruction and desolation of Judah laid out;

*Moreover I will take from them the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle.*

But, the Lord says through Jeremiah that His wrath will also come to the other nations of the region, utterly destroying them as well. Babylon as an empire serving as God's tool to pour out His wrath. And Judah will be captive 70 years, saith the Lord.

But God also tells us that this desolation and destruction will come to all nations. That God will recompense them according to their deeds. God judges nations by works, even as He offers salvation to individuals by faith.

And so God gives the prophet an understanding that the wine of His fury will be poured out against them all. Both literally the nations of Egypt and Uz and Moab and Edom and the rest, and as we read on, God swears His vengeance on every nation, in that great and terrible day of the Lord.

Even as Isaiah preached. And as the revelation of Jesus Christ gave to John about the future nation with the spirit of Babylon upon it, whose destruction parallels with the destruction of Jerusalem in Jeremiah's day:

*And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee*.

Even as all hope for God's repentance is lost and Jerusalem and the other mighty nations of the time cannot escape the judgment that's upon them, God gives the hope that His wrath against His people will be short lived, and He will eventually turn that wrath against Babylon, the nation that has its spirit upon it in the end times.

teachings.title: No freedom of religion in the Kingdom
teachings.summary: Conversion comes by the word and never the sword, so the Baptist distinctive of freedom from state religion is right, churches should be local, independent and Christ led, and a godly people should not allow false religions to be practiced.
teachings.text:
There is no "freedom of religion" in the Kingdom of Heaven. There is a right to individuals to choose not to believe. No one can force conversion by the sword, only by the word. But the allowance and practice of false religions should never be allowed by a Christian people.

The Baptist Distinctive regarding freedom from state religion is good, and right. A secular denomination with political power to force conversions will always create false gospels and result in persecution of believers. Churches should be local and independent, Christ led. Not top-down controlled by men.

A nation of believers should enforce this rule, destroying cults that worship other gods and lead others to apostasy. In my opinion.

But to have such a thing requires a godly people. The blessings of liberty are only bestowed on a nation when a large enough portion are at liberty in Christ.

Idolatrous sects, pagans, Jews, satanic cults, perverse groups who seek after other gods, rejecting the God of our fathers, should never have been given the freedom to spread their abominations.

There was a time when our forefathers understood that. The same people who wrote and adopted the Bill of Rights did not allow antichrist religions. Or at least tried not to. They blew it, in the end. And our people turned from God and now we suffer as a nation for it, making the point moot.

But this will be enforced in the Millennium. Amen.

teachings.title: Romans 13: living in godly subjection
teachings.theme: Subjection to the powers that be
teachings.summary: Believers are to submit to the authorities God ordains, obeying God rather than man only where they conflict, and trust God, for godly subjection is how God changes who rules over us.
teachings.text:
Romans 13 continues the theme of how saved Christians are to behave. It begins telling us God's view of earthly authority. Parents, bosses, civic leaders, law enforcement, all authorities under God, wicked and cruel or righteous and kind, to serve His will.

Of course we are to follow the higher law of God when earthly authority contradicts it. We are to obey God rather than man, but *if at all possible to live peaceably with all men*.

Many of us bristle at this. It requires our subjection and faith that God will protect and deliver us. Paying custom and tribute to people we know are wicked, stupid, foolish, deceitful is a hard thing to swallow. Not going into reactionary spirals. Not acting from fear. Honoring God by honoring those he's placed in authority over you. Starting with parents for children, husbands for wives, bosses for husbands.

When authority places you in conflict with God, meekly and in His name refuse, but attempt to offer a solution, even one that may harm your interests short term, that you may render what is acceptable to God and in doing so be rewarded long term.

This is so hard in our current year. But if it's fake and gay, can't be voted out, can't be fed posted, and God is with you anyways, what more can we do but live in Godly subjection? At worse be persecuted for His sake and be rewarded here and for eternity. At best be an example as to how God delivers His sons and daughters from tribulation so that others may believe, and in doing so change the nature of the people, turning them towards God. This is how the Bible teaches us we change who rules over us to a more benevolent or tolerable authority. It's how we win.

Hard lesson in faith.

teachings.title: Render to Caesar, and to God the things that are God's
teachings.summary: The point of Christ's answer is to render to God what is His; a people that does so gets better government, while Judea, refusing to repent, was destroyed.
teachings.text:
Continuing Mark 12.

The Pharisees who have decided they need to kill Jesus come tempting Him to say something rebellious against Roman occupation. They flatter Jesus and then ask if the Jews should pay taxes to the empire.

Jesus, in a verse even the godless heathens know, shows that Caesar is on the coin of the realm, and declares; *Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.*

The amount of discomfort and twisting of this doctrine by those whose love of money, the material, has kept them from rendering to God what is His for generations, in every Christian culture.

There is always the religious equivalent of Sovereign Citizens who balk at the idea of giving "their money" to the beast system. Here Jesus says it's not yours. It's not God's. It's the beast's and the beast exacts tribute. The point isn't even to pay your taxes, though you shouldn't care if you have to, but to RENDER TO GOD what is His.

If we as a nation, a people, willingly did that, the tax thing would take care of itself, because we get the government we deserve as a people. God judges nations.

The nation of Judea was 40yrs from its final destiny. God vowed to destroy it, and Jesus' prophesy came true and Judea destroyed, just like the unfaithful servants at the vineyard.

And it was in a fit of rebellion that the last of the Jews were crushed, following a false messianic figure in the **Bar Kokhba revolt,** 70 years after that.

What never occurred to these seditious and adulterous Jews was repentance to God and acceptance of Jesus as Christ.

They followed man and wrath and fear instead. They made it their idol. They worshipped themselves and despised God's longsuffering mercy on them.

This is how a people die. This is how a nation is judged. And rather than accept that and turn from their wicked ways and fear only the living God, Americans keep voting harder. And it is ironic that it was with resentment towards rendering unto Caesar that the Republicans gained power and acceptance as the outlet for supposed Christians to seek change, rather than change in their own hearts.

teachings.title: Not doing nothing: how a nation is healed
teachings.summary: A nation is healed not by sedition and outrage but by God's people humbling themselves, praying, obeying, raising godly families and winning souls (2 Chronicles 7:14).
teachings.text:
Unsaved men often criticize born again believers as "doing nothing," or that we are "weak," "afraid" or or "cowardly" because we aren't running around in panic, screaming in terror and getting sucked into reactionary spirals by the provocations and tribulations that the rulers of the darkness of this world, the spiritual wickedness in high places subject everyone to.

They rail and demand we join seditions and taking vengeance for ourselves. And they fail to notice that the more they do this, the worse the situation becomes for everyone. That they give those dark powers serving the god of this world justification for more cruelty, and make would-be allies among us more afraid of us than the wicked who oppress us.

This frustration, doubts and and impatience with God can strike even believing Christians.

But God is clear on how we save our nation and get His blessings for our people.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

Have faith. Obey the commandments. As much as possible live peaceably among men. Be a Godly husband, raise Godly children and share the gospel, winning souls. Give comfort to those morning, be a good judge for the fatherless and true widows.

This is not "doing nothing." It is hard work, or else it wouldn't be so difficult to get people to do it. Like most effective things, it requires discipline, motivation and perseverance. It's easier to express impotent outrage online.

The frustrations and provocations assailing us are how Satan tempts us, so he can accuse the saints before God. To make us sin over it, so that we can be persecuted for those sins by the powers that be. They want to avoid persecution of believers for His name's sake as much as possible, because they know that when they do, when they explicitly and clearly persecute us for our faith, directly, they lose.

The Bible says we suffer gladly for His sake we are rewarded here and in Heaven for it, and I can testify that at least as earthly rewards, it's true. And as a people, if Christians turn towards God and obeying Him, fearful for nothing except God, He will hear us and heal our land and brings blessings to all our nation, believers or not.

*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

teachings.title: There is no liberty outside of Christ
teachings.summary: True liberty comes only from salvation in Christ, not from any constitution, and only God blesses a nation through those who keep the faith.
teachings.text:
*Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage*.

This 4th of July, Independence Day, remember that the blessings of liberty come from the liberty found in Christ. There is no liberty outside of Christ.

It isn't an abstraction that can be grasped and measured. It isn't a concept to be understood and maintained in a secular setting. It has no meaning without the Gospel, the beautiful law of Liberty.

*But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.*

America secured the blessings of liberty through the faith of the founding stock. Not their masters. Not their king, not in the men that replaced him. Not in their documents. It isn't to be found in the Constitution. No parchment has or can grant liberty, or the blessings that come from it. Only salvation by grace through faith in Christ Jesus can.

And only God may bless those who maintain the faith and live it out, regardless of where or when.

And those blessings that abound to the faithful can continue and grow to the benefit of everyone in their nation, regardless of their faith. But the only way to secure those blessings is in the Lord;

*Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.*

teachings.title: The land vomiteth out her inhabitants
teachings.theme: The land spews out its inhabitants
teachings.summary: God judges nations for sexual perversion, idolatry and child sacrifice, and only turning from these sins heals the land.
teachings.text:
*Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you: And the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants.*

The judgment of God against nations is shown throughout the Bible. Here he tells us specifically the types of acts, sexual perversions, fornication, adultery, incest, beastiality, sodomy, that cause the land itself to visit the iniquity on the people, and spew them out. And it is these very acts that are promoted and encouraged on White, Western nations by the god of this world. The principalities, powers, and the rulers of the darkness of this world teach this spiritual wickedness.

These evils are pushed everywhere by Satan, who by his hatred of mankind seeks to damn us all. A ravening lion, seeking to devour us. But they are also weaponized by the enemy, to genocide a people. Again and again we see it in history, biblical and secular.

Child sacrifice, worshiping false gods, sodomy, sexual depravity. These are the causes of nations being destroyed.

It is only by turning from these sins that the land is healed and God repents of the evil He would visit upon a people.

teachings.title: God hates idols among His people
teachings.summary: Idol worship by those claiming His name, such as Catholics and Orthodox, provokes God's wrath and is a leading reason for the curses on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
It should go without saying that our God, Whose name is Jealous, and Who demands by His righteousness all the glory, hates Idolatry. He hates the veneration and worship of idols, *especially* by those claiming to be of His people. The Second Commandment is again hammered home here in the opening verse;

*Ye shall make you no idols nor graven image, neither rear you up a standing image, neither shall ye set up any image of stone in your land, to bow down unto it: for I am the Lord your God.*

Those who call themselves by His name who bow before statues of stone, standing images and molten and graven idols, are what spark His wrath.

Catholicism and Orthodox Christianity, so called, the apostates who reject salvation by grace, and set up images to be served and bowed before in supplication, are the leading reason why Europe and America are suffering today. Why these curses and others spelled out by God throughout the Old Testament, are afflicting our land today.

When Asa became king and *he took away the sodomites out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made*, the Bible says he did what was right in the eyes of the Lord.

If we were to have a return to doing what was right in the eyes of the Lord, we who are His people would need to destroy every image and idol, from the blasphemy of St. Patrick's Cathedral, to every profane "crucifix," to every bathtub Mary in every Catholic yard, throughout the land.

teachings.title: The potter's power over nations
teachings.summary: The potter of Jeremiah 18 and Romans 9 is about nations, as God destroys some to show His wrath and His mercy on others, as with the Jews and Gentiles.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 18** begins a shift in the narrative structure, where for the past several chapters Jeremiah had made some effort to plead with God to not be too hard on Judah, and God explaining that they've condemned their own selves with their fornication, going after false gods. Not heeding the word of God from the prophets but following the vain jangling from the false prophets telling the people that they were fine and judgment wasn't coming. That they were at peace with God. Even as they burned incense to idols and baked cakes to the "queen of heaven."

But chapter 18 begins with God sending Jeremiah to observe a potter, who is spinning the wheel to turn clay into a vessel. And, seeing the potter discard a bowl that didn't turn out right, to make another that would.

While many take the potter analogy and make it about us as individuals, because God does shape us to be fitted for His purpose, the primary application here, and in **Romans 9**, is about nations, specifically the physical nation of Israel. The descendants of Abraham.

*O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter? saith the Lord. Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel. At what instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy it*.

As Paul writes, nearly 8 centuries later;

*Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour? What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: And that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory*.

We see that the context remains the same. The destruction of the Jews serves God's purpose, that His wrath be manifest, but also His glory in those raised up in His mercy, the Gentiles.

God's judgment against Egypt and Pharaoh allowed His mercy to be seen in the children of Israel. His destruction of the northern kingdom, as a warning to Judah in the south. Judah's destruction by the Babylonians that Jeremiah is preaching will allow God to be glorified in their eventual return. The final destruction of the Jews in their rejection of Christ opens the door to the Gentiles to be graft in.

God uses the judgment against nations to bring about the glory of His mercy to those that believe. His wrath revealed from heaven allows His mercy and grace to be manifest in those He will be saved in His son.

teachings.title: Peter sent to Cornelius
teachings.summary: As with the eunuch and Saul, God sent a man to preach to Cornelius, and God being no respecter of persons in the gospel does not undo His hierarchies or the nations and borders He sets.
teachings.text:
Now we find in Acts 10 the story of Cornelius, a Roman centurion stationed in Samaria, in the port city of Caesarea and someone who was devout to God, but not saved. Praying and giving alms, God-fearing and fasting, but in ignorance of the truth of the gospel. And God, seeing his searching for truth sends him a vision of an angel telling him to send men to bring Peter to him, that "*he shall tell thee what thou oughtest do.*"Just as the Lord tells Saul in chapter 9 to wait on Ananias.

And, similarly to Philip in chapter 8 with the Ethiopian eunuch and Ananias to Saul in 9, we see God telling Peter to go unto Cornelius.

This is important. Things God repeats we should pay attention to. The angels and visions and even the glorified appearance of Jesus, none give the gospel but rather send saved men to preach the word and get other men saved. We are called to be ministers of reconciliation, that we may save some. Don't miss this point, for it applies as much today as it did here. It is by man acting as agents for God, a royal priesthood sharing the Gospel, that by hearing man may come to believe.

Peter is in Joppa, and sees a vision from God showing every type of animal, clean and unclean according to Masoretic law, and God tells him to slay and eat. Peter, that stone, protests saying he has never eaten an unclean thing. God, using this illustration to show Peter he must preach to the Gentiles, says nothing is unclean if God has cleansed it.

This is an allegory for preaching to the Gentiles, but it also serves as a reminder that the carnal ordinances and dietary laws that were a picture of the better Testament to come are done away with in Christ. That no meat is unlawful for a saved Christian to eat, that is blessed by God.

It's interesting that the vision is repeated to Peter 3 times before he wakes from it. Just as Peter denied Christ 3 times and as he was instructed by the risen Jesus 3 times to feed His sheep. God repeats things he wants us to understand, and Peter is no different than us in his being slow on the uptake sometimes.

The messengers sent by Cornelius arrive as Peter comes out of his vision, and understanding through the Spirit that he is to go with them,

Cornelius, who anticipating Peter's arrival has gathered not just his household, but his kinsmen and close friends, falls to Peter's feet and worships him, but is rebuked by the Apostle. "I am just a man."

Peter, now in a household full of Gentiles, who being in Palestine and living among Jews, mentions to the gathered that under Jewish custom he was forbidden from doing what he is doing, but that God's vision had shown him differently.

Peter says he understands now that God is not a respecter of persons.

Neither should we be when it comes to the Gospel, and serving our brothers in Christ. There are no men of any race or ethnicity to whom we should think they are unclean in the spirit of giving the Gospel. This isn't as universalist as it is portrayed. We should treat every human being as we would have them treat us, and in matters of God, rich or poor, bond or free, Jew or Greek, man or woman, all the same in Christ.

This does not however do away with our hating the wicked who hate God, the hierarchy of rule given by God for the powers that be; child to mother to husband to God, congregants to deacons to pastors to Christ, paying custom and tribute to those who rule, with God above all. And the establishment of nations and borders, which are drawn and redrawn by God to His purpose. This is not being a respecter of persons but rather respecting God and His Judgement. Too few understand this and in their ignorance and pride, err one way or the other in this, following their own judgement instead.

teachings.title: Not sedition but faith in God
teachings.summary: As unbelieving Jerusalem neared judgment, believers needed not take up arms but trust God to judge in His time, for persecution makes His people flourish and fear dims our light.
teachings.text:
This all is taking place roughly 58-60AD. The political situation in Judea and among the Jews of Samaria is getting strained and rebellion is growing. This untoward generation of unbelieving Jews is rapidly approaching its judgement, the Jewish war of 66, followed by the desolation of Jerusalem scattering the remnant of Jews of the flesh and total destruction of the temple in 70AD. It's a fascinating dynamic, and Jesus' and His apostles and believers impact on the hastening of these events is obvious.

We need not sow sedition or take up arms or anything else but have faith in God. Turning towards Him, trusting He will judge the nation using His means for His wrath in His time.

Often Christians get impatient with God and His long-suffering, and eager for their perception of justice, try to take vengeance into their own hands. Their lack of faith and sin of fear grips them, and desperation fueled by provocation and deliberate humiliation is used by the enemy to tempt us. To have us turn away from God and towards an earthly solution. Reactionary spirals, further worsening the conditions we face. Dancing to the devil's tune. Slaves to Satan's plans.

Tribulation and persecution is a part of the Christian life. The Bible promises us that as believers we will be hated of the world, because the world hates Him. That the greater things we do for God, the harsher the persecution. And, as we see through out the Bible, and in history, the more God's people are persecuted in His name, the more His people flourish.

*For we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

And knowing this, how can we be fearful? And being fearful, how can we be a light that shines? How can we *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you?*

Paul has been scourged repeatedly. Scared by stripes. Stoned to death and raised immediately. Chased out of countries, driven from cities. Plotted against and arrested multiple times.

And like when he was held in a Philippian jail, singing songs and Psalms of praise to God for it.

God has written to us to be not afraid 365 times in His word, once verse for every day of the year, and yet so many Christians live in misery and despair. They hide their light under a bushel, while the faithful shine it to beggars and princes alike.

teachings.title: Obey masters and powers as unto God
teachings.summary: Children, servants, wives and subjects should honour authority even when it is harsh, unless commanded to sin, working diligently and blamelessly because they serve God.
teachings.text:
The final chapter of Ephesians, Paul continues to build on the idea that we are not to despise government, the hierarchies put in place by God, but to honor and respect them, even when they are cruel to us. For we aren't theirs, but God's and what we do in our labors is His.

Be it a husband, a mother, a child, a master or a servant, a king or a subject. If they aren't demanding we sin, truly sin in the despising of God, worship of idols or the blasphemy of the Spirit, and the like, we should in all good conscience work that which we can do, upright. This bothers many.

"How can I obey and serve a cruel and ungodly master? A wicked husband? Dishonorable parents? A beast-system state?" The Bible tells us with faith, meekness, serving God and by our actions, convert the lost.

I find that those that bristle the most at this were raised without proper fear and respect for their parents, due to whatever reason, although mostly having the rod spared or worse, used in anger, bringing their children to wrath. And as the relationship with the father goes, so to becomes their relationship with all superiors, and in the end, their relationship with God.

We should, as Christians, seek to be blameless. Be the hardest worker at your job. Be the most honest. Take the least advantage and support and uplift others, not being a respecter of persons. Diligent and happy. Having faith in God who rewards us, Paul says, *Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free.*

This is not weakness, but strength. For the powers that be have authority from God, be they wicked or just, those who bear the sword do it to the fear of the unrighteous.

**1 Peter 3**, which echos this sentiment, shows us how regardless the situation, we win:

*13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?*

*14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;*

Or **2 Peter 2**:

*4 For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;*

*5 And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;*

*6 And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;*

*7 And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:*

*8 (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

*9 The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:*

*10 But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.*

teachings.title: Render unto God the things that are God's
teachings.summary: Jesus turned the tribute question to show the Pharisees did not give God His due, and the worldly fixate on the Caesar half while the spiritual see the call to render unto God.
teachings.text:
Now, offended by His preaching, the Pharisees attempt to trap Jesus in sedition against Rome. They send their disciples and the Hellenistic Jews, the Herodians, who with flattery ask Jesus to judge whether it is right under the law to give tribute to Caesar. For Jews to pay taxes to the empire that occupied them.

Jesus annoyed at their deception, knowing the wickedness they sought to do, says;

*Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?*

*Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?*
*They say unto him, Caesar's.*

*Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.*

Often the focus here is mistakenly on Jesus saying to render unto Caesar what is Caesar's, which is true. We should, as much as possible, live peaceably with all men, giving tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom is due. Materialistic things are the provence of the world.

But Jesus is turning the question around on those tempting Him, that their focus should be on the spiritual. That they do not pay tribute to God as they should. They do not render unto God that which is His due.

This exchange can serve almost as a Rorschach test, where the more worldly a person, the more they focus on what Christ says about the things of Caeser, debating taxes and obedience to earthly law, tributes and custom, be they worldly liberals talking about social contracts and socialism, or worldly "sovereign citizens," and their false gospel of libertarianism and sedition.

Those who are more spiritual, looking to the Kingdom, see the focus on giving God His due, which the Pharisees and their disciples were slacking, as so many calling themselves Christian today are, too.

teachings.title: Servants honouring masters for a good witness
teachings.summary: Scripture repeatedly commands obeying earthly authority and being the best of workers so God's name is not blasphemed, while always keeping God as the higher authority and leaving wrath to Him.
teachings.text:
The final chapter in 1st Timothy, and it is building on the theme of being able to give a good testimony for Christ to others by living like you have the gift of eternal life, not stuck in the cares of this world but growing in spirit.

The admonition to obey earthly authority, to please God and make His glory seen of man that you may give a good witness is repeated throughout the New Testament, from Jesus rendering unto Caesar, to Romans 13 and 1 Peter 2, and elsewhere. This is one of the hardest doctrines for most American Christians today, spoiled by the supposed promises of "Liberty" from the Constitution, and missing the liberty we have in Christ.

We bristle with pride at the idea of being good servants at work, living agreeably with all men as much as possible, paying taxes, tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom. Honor to parents and elders. This doctrine is seen as being a "Christ cuck." Seen as weak by those lacking understanding. Missing that while we defer to authority, we have roles of authority in God's hierarchy ourselves, and that we are instructed to always place God and His word as our final authority.

Often those who cry loudest about supposed persecution and calls for riot and seditions, have abandoned their own roles, or are derelict in their own responsibilities. They care more for their comfort than for their testimony. They live in fear rather than faith. They see wrath as theirs, not God's.

They, not being satisfied with what God has given them, and impatient with His longsuffering, are unable to bring others to believe and so, shoot themselves in the foot and worsen their own condition.

We have one means to lead a nation back from wickedness, and that is the Gospel. Soul winning. Revival. And that requires our being good witnesses to the power of the Spirit and faith that God, who is holy and just, and will keep His promise and restore us.

Paul is writing to Timothy who, living in Macedonia, a slave/caste society, will have gotten both masters and slaves saved, and in the same congregation. We are blessed not to be living in a society that openly enslaves people. But the same admonition applies to us as wage-slaves.

Be the best employee at your job. Even if your boss is terrible. Your employer, even if he despises religion and doesn't know Christ should still be forced by your witness to see Christians as good employees. The best, because we work for God not them. Those of us *under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.*

We represent Christ to the world. We are to be a light that draws men near.

And again, this isn't to say if a manager calls on you to do something that is contrary to God's word that you have to submit. We defer to the higher authority and there is none higher than God. But we do it peaceably, and with humility and meekness, trusting in God to save us should it lead to persecution.

We don't obey to avoid being persecuted, but to please God, and with the full expectation that we might face tribulation when we defer to God's will over earthly authority.

Paul uses Jesus' own example before Pilate, which by His meek silence led to Pilate confessing He was blameless, and leading to the Glory of God in the crucifixion.

*But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.*

teachings.title: Even the dogs received the crumbs
teachings.summary: Jesus came to take away the sins of the whole world, so salvation is by individual faith and not by flesh and blood, while God judges nations by their collective works.
teachings.text:
I was posting commentary on the Gentile woman who comes to Jesus asking Him to cast The devil out of her daughter, and His telling her that until the children were full, the dogs shouldn't be fed.

Her clever retort that even the dogs catch crumbs as they fall to the floor moves Jesus to mercy and he heals her daughter. This showed both the faith of the woman, and her ability to hear and understand Jesus's parable.

He wasn't literally calling Gentiles dogs in a derogatory way, he was making a point that his earthly ministry was to the Lost tribes of Israel, the sheep that needed to be gathered back to their master.

By showing ears to hear, and understanding she showed that she hears her master's voice.

Many dispensationalists and Jews use these passages and their parallel in other Gospels, to promote a wicked idea that Jesus was for the Jews, and that the conversion of the Gentiles later by the Great Commission was some sort of special boy thing.

Jesus came on his earthly ministry to those who had been given the oracles of god, the words of the prophet, the law written out not just in their hearts but in stone and in parchment, published about. That they should have recognized Him for who He is, the Christ, before He was lifted up on the cross, calling all men unto redemption.

To them much was given. *What advantage then hath the Jew?* This is that advantage.

But in all things, in all ways, Jesus was sent to take away the sins of the whole world.

Now there are many theories as to who represents the true tribes of Israel, and who the Jews who say they are but are not might be. I am not ignorant of them, and I have my own theories and preferences regarding this, that match what many of you believe. But the striving and debate that surround these theories often venture too close to foolish genealogies and Jewish fables. Some of which are a Kaiser Sose effort by Jews to cloud their origin and past, making them out to be more powerful or sinister than they can be. And ideas promoted by others who wish to make salvation one of blood rather than faith, of flesh rather than spirit. This is a huge mistake.

We have individual soul liberty. We are freed in Christ one by one, by a free will faith. And we are also damned by that same free will when we choose not to obey the gospel. And some, not wishing to retain God in their knowledge while here on Earth make the free will choice to harden their hearts and are turned over, given up to reprobation.

Now, some are blessed to be born into a nation of peoples whose hearts are inclined to the Lord.  To us is given the oracles of God. To be born in a Christian majority nation is an advantage similar to that of the Jew in the first century compared to the Greek.

Today we have this advantage over China, India or Israel. And though many of us fail to come to saving faith in Christ, none of our nation is ignorant to his existence and the good news of His resurrection. Amen.

And just as some of us are blessed to be born into a nation inclined towards God, some are born into a nation that so utterly rejects Him, that there are few seeking to find Him.

God judges nations by their collective works, here on earth. He judges man by their faith, individually, for the Kingdom to come.

It is not by flesh and blood that we are saved, but by faith and spirit. Never lose sight of that, regardless of what theory you hold. Even the dogs received the crumbs.

teachings.title: God judges nations; Jewish identity is rejecting Christ
teachings.summary: God is no respecter of persons in offering salvation but judges nations collectively, and the Jews' identity rests on rejecting Christ, so they are given over as in Romans 1.
teachings.text:
God is not a respecter of persons, the Bible says repeatedly. He does not care if you are great or small, rich or poor. Man or woman, Greek or Jew, where you're from or who your parents are. He gives us all the same offer of salvation and adoption in Christ. As individuals we have free will.

God does judge nations. He does favor some over others at times, and destroys many who go too far astray. He curses the land stained by blood of violence. Sodomy. Fornication. Of people, collectively, to the fourth generation.

We are to know the judgment of God and emulate it. Not being a respecter of persons, giving the Gospel to whomever we meet, but judging ungodly nations for what they are. Including our own.
