Every nation carries that burden, where the godly among them must turn towards God so that He may heal their land. Not just ours.

Jews, from the most Orthodox to the most liberal Reformed to the atheists, all draw their identity not of blood, (none can tell you their tribe or origin), not of true ethnicity. They draw their identity directly from rejecting Christ Jesus as the Messiah, and having not the Son, have not the Father. Being liars who are antichrists. Being reprobate IS their identity.

No other nation or ethnicity is founded on this lie and pride in rejecting God.

And because they don't wish to retain God in their knowledge, *He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.*

And so, Romans 1 applies to them as it applies to all that go the way of the Pharoah.

teachings.title: Not cucked: Paul's subjection and boldness
teachings.summary: Being subject to the powers, living peaceably and leaving vengeance to God is not weakness, for Paul and the apostles submitted while boldly preaching the truth even unto chains and death.
teachings.text:
I was just struck with a realization about the irony of those who call Christianity "cucked," and who attempt to discredit the writings of the Apostle Paul based on his Epistles regarding the behavior of Christians, especially relative to the powers that be. To the government. Being subject to those who have power over us, given by God. To, as much as possible, live at peace with all men. Romans 13, etc.

The irony being that Paul was subject to constant persecution, was stoned to death at one point, had to be snuck out of cities in baskets least the mobs led by Jews tear him apart, and who wrote a majority of his epistles from chains. Literally bound for preaching the word of God and the gospel of Christ crucified.

We are instructed by the Bible to not riot in the daytime or take vengeance for ourselves. To render custom to who is due custom and tribute to who is due tribute. Pastors to subject themselves to Jesus, servants to their masters, husbands to loving their wives as Christ loves His brethren, wives to be subject to their husbands and children to honor their parents. To render unto Caesar that which is Caesars. To pay our taxes and obey the laws so long as they do not contradict the authority of the Lord and His word.

To have faith that God will save us from tribulation and persecution. To allow God to exact vengeance for us. To glory in our persecution for His name's sake. This isn't being "cucked," it's literally the only way we win.

And Paul, who wrote much of this from a jail cell, under house arrest, bound to a centurion by chains 24 hours a day for the cause of Christ, saw no contradiction in any of that.

As long as you're preaching the word of God, you shouldn't worry about things like hate crime laws or censorship, or any other persecution led by the Jews. Glory in your affliction and speak the truth.

In Acts, Peter, James, Paul and others are openly condemned and set up on for vocally pointing out that the Jews were antichrists who killed Christ Jesus. Stephen was martyred for "hate speech" against the Jews.

These meek and humble servants, who turned the world upsidedown with their preaching, drew a line in the sand.

They turned the other cheek, loved their enemies, heaping coals upon the heads of those who hated them by their charity and humble conversation. Living peaceably.

But when it came to the preaching of the word and the truth of those who hate Christ, they boldly spoke out, despite threats of jail, and even unto death.

Would that we are blessed by God with so strong a faith.

teachings.title: Jethro's counsel to delegate judgment
teachings.summary: God approves delegated authority, so believers should know His word for themselves, with fathers, pastors and deacons answering to Christ, a pattern of the Millennial kingdom.
teachings.text:
But regardless of all that, and regardless of the marriage troubles Moses may have had, Jethro in his visit gives good advice to his son-in-law Moses.

Moses has 600,000 men, plus women and children in the mixed multitudes encamped with him. 12 tribes of Israel, come out of Egypt, and as their leader, he must sit in judgment. Jethro observes the long lines and the grind of dealing with them all that Moses faces and offers good advice.

*The thing that thou doest is not good.*
*Thou wilt surely wear away, both thou, and this people that is with thee: for this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.*
*Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God: And thou shalt teach them ordinances and laws, and shalt shew them the way wherein they must walk, and the work that they must do. Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God, men of truth, hating covetousness; and place such over them, to be rulers of thousands, and rulers of hundreds, rulers of fifties, and rulers of tens: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee. If thou shalt do this thing, and God command thee so, then thou shalt be able to endure, and all this people shall also go to their place in peace.*

God blesses this arrangement, and Moses takes to it and does as Jethro advised.

We see other times, in other places throughout the Bible that God approves of delegation of authority. He wants the people to know His ways and laws and the ordinances of remembrance, that in what they do they know the next right choice to make.

We are to know the word of God that we can know ourselves what His will is. Without needing someone micromanaging and interpreting scripture, to constantly make decisions for us on normal matters.

God then sets up captains over people, to judge matters for their people. By 10s, 100s and 1,000s. And a leader who answers to God, for the tougher matters of judgment. Thus will it be in the Millennium. Those who showed judgment and did great things for the Lord will be given much in the Kingdom. Those good and faithful servants will be made rulers, as Jesus described in the parable of the servants.

We see the wisdom in this arrangement. The way it maximizes the ability to serve God and edify people. And this exists today through God's word; the priesthood of believers, the husband/father of the home, the local pastor, his helpers the deacons or elders, all answering to Jesus. It is the form of Christian nationalism that we should seek.

teachings.title: Thou shalt not bow down to graven images
teachings.summary: Idolatry is still sin, and Catholic kneeling, candles and processions before images are worship of idols, a key reason God's wrath is on America and Europe.
teachings.text:
Just a side note, the New Testament commands we flew idols. That Idolatry is still a sin. *Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold* still stands.

*Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.*

Note also, that this commandment, which Catholics omit from their version, for obvious reasons, has 'bowing down,' the literal meaning of worship. Those kneeling before idols are worshiping. Those lighting a candle in front of them are serving. The feasts of the "saints," where the people carry an idol through the streets, and give service unto it are a blasphemy.

And God promises to strike a nation, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon them unto the third and fourth generation.

If you want to know one of the prime reasons God's wrath is upon the United States, and Europe, it is for allowing this blasphemy to continue for 1500yrs.

teachings.title: The law failed because men failed
teachings.summary: The law failed to produce righteousness because Israel would not execute its judgments, and God's wrath abides on any nation that refuses His statutes.
teachings.text:
We know the law is made to be a schoolmaster to bring Israel to repentance of faith in the Christ to come. That the failing of the law to achieve righteousness wasn't God's fault, but man's.

Because when a man dishonored his father and mother, cursing them, the people didn't put him to death.

Because when a man committed adultery with his neighbor's wife, they weren't put to death.

When a man committed incest, uncovering the nakedness of his own family's women, commiting abominations, the people do not put him to death.

When sodomites were found amongst them, men laying with men, abominations to the Lord, the people suffered them to live rather than stoning them to death, their blood being upon them.

Beastiality, incest, the abomination of sex in the blood of menstruation...all these things that God warns nations about eventually are left unchecked by a wicked and perverse generation. The people didn't follow His statutes.

*Ye shall therefore keep all my statutes, and all my judgments, and do them: that the land, whither I bring you to dwell therein, spue you not out. And ye shall not walk in the manners of the nation, which I cast out before you: for they committed all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.*

God's wrath abides on a nation that fails to sanctify themselves through his  statutes and judgments. As the nations driven out before the Isralites were condemned. As Israel itself would be. And as nations even to this day find out as the land spews them out for their abominations.

teachings.title: Eye for eye is God's law, not Hammurabi's
teachings.summary: Eye for eye is God's just law for magistrates, while Jesus calls believers personally to mercy, and the two are complementary rather than contradictory.
teachings.text:
The second half of the chapter begins with a narrative of a child of Egyptian heritage born into the Tribe of Dan, blaspheming God, and God's instructions to take him without the camp and those who heard the blasphemy to stone him to death.

God reiterates that even strangers among them are under His law, both to their good, and to their punishment for violating it.

He says His law is justice, that a murderer be put to death. That blemish, or physical harm, be answered in a like manner; breach for breach, eye for eye, tooth for tooth.

This concept of God's law has been understood for millennia, preserved for all time, but in 1901 a Babylonian relic was found that contained what is called Hammurabi's Code, a list of laws credited to the ancient king by archeologists, which included the eye for an eye form of justice.

During the 20th century, what was part of God's perfect law (repeated from **Exodus 21:24-25**
*Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot*, *Burning for burning, wound for wound, stripe for stripe*) began to be credited to a man, and after it had permeated culture that the concept of an eye for an eye actually originated from Hammurabi's Code, people began to mistakenly think it wasn't God's perfect law. And once they'd managed to mislead people with that, they then began to discredit the concept as barbaric, a remnant of ancient Babylon and not the commandments of God.

And so by the close of the 20th Century, most people had no idea that this was found in scripture, and were taught to think of it as a savage injustice.

If the concept was raised by Christians at all, it was in the context of **Matthew 5:38-39**; *Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.* And this was taught as somehow Jesus contradicting the concept, as if He wasn't the author of it. When Jesus says love thy neighbor, The same people pretend it was a new commandment when it comes from Leviticus as well.

But Jesus calling those who are saved by faith in Him to love even our enemies, to pray for them, to not answer violence with violence, but to show mercy and love to them, isn't saying that the law itself is unjust, for it will be the law in the Millennial Kingdom. He's talking about our hearts storing up wrath, vengeance, and hatred.

Before a magistrate, the eye taken for an eye would still be justice.

**1 Timothy 1:9-11**
*Knowing this, that the law is not made for a righteous man, but for the lawless and disobedient, for the ungodly and for sinners, for unholy and profane, for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, for manslayers, For whoremongers, for them that defile themselves with mankind, for menstealers, for liars, for perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is contrary to sound doctrine; According to the glorious gospel of the blessed God, which was committed to my trust.*

But we who are righteous should forgive those who wronged us and show mercy to those in need. These two concepts aren't contradictory but complimentary.

Our mercy doesn't upend the law. Our being at liberty from the law spiritually means we should be more circumspect in how we view our enemies. Our trust in God for vengeance taking priority over our executing our own wrath.

But if the law demands restitution, so be it. The sword is not wielded in vain.

What those who seek to undermine confidence in scripture do is trust that Christians won't be able to rightly divide the word of God, and this higher level concept would escape us, and lead us to showing perverse judgment.

If you notice, by abandoning the law for the unrighteous, instead of mercy and love and limited restitution to a like-for-like code, we have a "justice system" that either punishes the wrong doer far exceeding what is right in the eyes of God, or not doing anything to rightly punish the wicked and protect the innocent. Those that deserve death still live, often freed to offend again.

teachings.title: Justice in the world, meekness in the believer
teachings.summary: Believers must be meek peacemakers personally while God's law should still be upheld by the state, and ignoring this has left society with neither justice nor mercy.
teachings.text:
The nuance required to understand these differences, The worldly application of biblical principles with people who aren't believers versus how believers should respond personally. This causes confusion for many in other applications such as application of Romans 13 and 14.

Christians are called to be meek, to be peacemakers, to be humble in realizing that our condition is by the grace of God and not of ourselves. To be understanding of our enemies that by love, we may overcome it and bring them to the same peace that we have found in the grace of God.

But that doesn't mean that in this world, God's law shouldn't be upheld. And if we were to stone to death, someone for a capital violation, We should not do so gleefully and with vengeance but with understanding. And after applying just mercy.

By not walking this line, we have a society wherein there is no justice and there is no mercy.

We have courts that are grossly unfair. We have a criminal justice system that can't decide between rehabilitation and punishment and so attains neither.

We don't put to death those who have their own blood upon them. And we lock up people who could have simply worked off the harm they caused. The application of the law becomes arbitrary and capricious rather than circumspect and done with discernment.

teachings.title: Woe to them that join house to house
teachings.summary: God's jubilee law forbade usury and the hoarding of land, a fair system neither capitalist nor communist that kept families and tribes intact and still shows how to live.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 5:8**
*Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!*

God hates unfair dealings, taking advantage of others for profit, especially in their poverty. Unjust weights and measures. Mistreatment of servants. Usury among His people and the accumulation of property and capital, to the exclusion of others.

Basically, Capitalism.

But that is not to say He endorsed Communism, either. But fair and righteous trade and checks on over accumulation of wealth, or subjugation of His people. Productive enterprise and free markets (little f, little m), were the way He provided.

This system was fair and just and kept in remembrance of God being who we rely on, who provides for all. Rich or poor, servant or free.

The right of return to their own place, the inheritance they claim, enabled the genealogies to be recorded, and kept the tribes separated as He had ordained through the lots when it was eventually divided.

It kept the integrity of nations, as a people, as kin.

The genealogies also then served a purpose, bringing us to Christ's human family being perfect in its generations as it is given in the Gospel. And the real jubilee being the ultimate sabbath, which is Jesus.

The elegance and perfection of this law shouldn't be lost in the allegory or spiritual application, however. It really is the way that we should live, even today.

teachings.title: The covenant kept in Christ, not in the Jews
teachings.summary: Leviticus 26's remedy of confession is fulfilled in Christ, and God's Israel is believers circumcised in heart, while unbelieving Jews remain under the curse.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 26** is one of the many times God reiterates the warning to Israel, that if they don't keep the conditions of the covenant God has made with them, he will curse them 7-fold, remove them from the land and set their enemies up over them.

This held specific meaning to the Hebrews in the wilderness, entering into Canaan, but it is true of all people who call themselves by His name.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

The curse against His people comes with a remedy. Because the Lord is a forgiving and merciful God.

*If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me; And that I also have walked contrary unto them, and have brought them into the land of their enemies; if then their uncircumcised hearts be humbled, and they then accept of the punishment of their iniquity: Then will I remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.*

(Note the physical circumcision availa them nothing. It is the circumcision of the heart, made without hands, in Christ Jesus;

*In whom also ye are circumcised with the circumcision made without hands, in putting off the body of the sins of the flesh by the circumcision of Christ*.
...
*But he is a Jew, which is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the spirit, and not in the letter; whose praise is not of men, but of God.*)

This covenant is and always has been kept in Christ. It was to Abraham's seed, who is Jesus, and those blessings fall on those adopted into the promise by faith in Him. Those calling themselves Jews today *could* repent to be partakers of the promise, but note that they'd have to admit not only that they forsook God and didn't walk in His statutes, rejecting Christ, and deserved their punishments, but they'd have to also testify that God has walked contrary to them, and that His judgment was right.

In the various captivites and tribulations of the OT Israelites, this repentance led to their being restored. But modern Jews, so-called, maintain in their being scattered, in their being cursed, in their being kept from peace in the land, they keep the fiction that they remain God's chosen people. That they aren't being cursed for their unbelief, but that it is we who believe, those circumcised of the heart, who afflict them unjustly.

*And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies; and the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them; and they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.*

This is seen in the ADL and the cries of "antisemetism," seeing swastikas and threats of genocide in construction markings and preaching from the Bible. The wicked flee where none pursue. They are faint of heart, as the Lord promises.

Talmudic rabbinical Judasism shows that they despise God's statutes and abhor His judgements, so that they do not keep His commandments but instead find loopholes and rationalizations in the vain traditions of men, doctrines they invented taught as commandments of God.

His tabernacle is not set in their midst, who is Jesus. They are contrary to all men. God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost.

God's people, Israel, has always been a nation of believers who, by faith, carry the circumcision of the heart. Today it is believing Christians, and our nations are blessed by the few within it who keep the word of God, and cursed when we who call ourselves by His name reject His judgement.

teachings.title: God gives many chances, then judgment
teachings.summary: God warns nations, backsliders and the lost again and again, but after rote religion and wickedness continue, His judgment comes and He forbids intercession.
teachings.text:
The preaching of the word of God continues, Jeremiah prophesying in the Spirit that God is casting His judgment upon a wicked and perverse generation of Judah.

As He frequently does, the Lord, being long-suffering and full of mercy and grace, extends His hand first. Saying; *Amend your ways and your doings, and I will cause you to dwell in this place.*

Because the judgment of nations is done on this earth. And the wickedness of those who are His people will be met with the rod of correction and reproof.

We serve the living God and as His sons, the spiritual seed of Abraham, we too face this judgment for our inequity and the inequity of the people.

But, because of His love, grace is always available to those sons who repent. The prodigal who returns home. The nation where the people who call themselves by His name turn back towards Him, God promises to heal.

God instructs Jeremiah to preach at the door of the temple, to those in Judah entering in for sacrifice and burnt offerings, but who outside the temple blaspheme God. Serving other gods. Commiting wickedness; they
*steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not*, and yet out of habit and vain faith they return to His temple to do the performative religious acts, that do not save them.

*Is this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, even I have seen it, saith the Lord.*

This is the scripture Jesus preaches during His scourging of the moneychangers in the Temple;

**Matthew 21:13**
*And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.*

It's the same spirit that gripped the Pharisses, rote practices of ordinances but nothing given to the weightier matters of the law;

**Matthew 23:23**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone*

God says He has spoken to them, warning them, calling out to repent and they didn't hear. *They answered not.*

When God says this, He obviously means it literally, that through the prophets He has instructed His people and warned them, but more; He had recently allowed the entire Northern Kingdom, and the 10 tribes therein, to be destroyed and scattered by the Assyrians, for just such behavior. The whole seed of Ephraim, being the most prominent tribe of Israel, represents those northern 10 tribes. He reminds them "I have cast out all of thy brethren."

God gives His people chances. Repeatedly. He gives unsaved people multiple chances as well. The Spirit moving to rebuke the world that they may come to believe. But eventually, be it judgment upon a nation that is destroyed, judgment against a backslidden believer where they are rebuked and eventually called home if they don't respond, or to the unbelievers who don't wish to retain God in their knowledge, and are made reprobate. God gives us multiple chances and warnings to repent towards Him and His mercies.

God says to Jeremiah, don't even bother praying for intercession. He is done with these people. This is on them, their last chance.

teachings.title: Jeremiah teaches us to face a nation's judgment
teachings.summary: Jeremiah and Lamentations prepare believers to be at peace when judgment falls on their nation, trusting God's perfect will and His promised deliverance.
teachings.text:
Now we're there in chapter 14 of Jeremiah and we see a continuation of what has become the pattern over the past few chapters, that Jeremiah is beseeching the Lord for mercy for his people while the Lord preaches through Jeremiah to them about their sin. And especially the judgment that has come upon them.

As it goes, we see Jeremiah becoming more desperate in pleading the case for the children of Israel. And we see God has hardened His heart against them. He is promising that they shall die by famine and by sword and be carried away captive into a strange land. God's mind is set upon this judgment and His wrath is upon them.

In chapter 14, we see Jeremiah begging not to do this to the people who call themselves by his name, Who are his people. And God says don't even bother praying for them. They can't make burnt offerings or fast enough for Him to repent. Reprobate, silver shellman call them because the Lord has given up on them.

Again, the parallels to today are striking. And again, we should remind ourselves that in all times and places there have been Jeremiah's. And there have been people who have done wickedly and received the just wrath of God.

Part of the  reason for the book of Jeremiah and lamentations that follow is to help set us in the right frame of mind and understanding when tribulation comes to our nations. When the wickedness of our people leads us to destruction. That we can be at peace with it even as we preach hard against it. Hoping that our people turn back to the Lord.

Much like Job and understanding how God deals with us as individuals, Even we who are righteous in His name.

But also like Job. It is easy to empathize and feel the emotion as they go through their trials and tribulations. The frustration of it. But it's humbling to understand that God's will is not our will. And God's point of view is outside of time and perfect while we see through a glass darkly. Our faith should be bolstered by reading this because we know how it turned out in the end. And we know how Israel was delivered by Christ and the resurrection promised in the scriptures by a God who cannot lie. And so we should take comfort in that as the people who call ourselves by His name. As we await a better country.

teachings.title: Idolatry and reprobate nations
teachings.summary: Nations that turn to idolatry behave as Romans 1 describes and are given over to God's judgment, as the Canaanites and Israel were, and Catholic and Orthodox idolatry has brought that same judgment on Europe and America.
teachings.text:
*Take heed unto yourselves, lest ye forget the covenant of the Lord your God, which he made with you, and make you a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, which the Lord thy God hath forbidden thee. For the Lord thy God is a consuming fire, even a jealous God. When thou shalt beget children, and children's children, and ye shall have remained long in the land, and shall corrupt yourselves, and make a graven image, or the likeness of any thing, and shall do evil in the sight of the Lord thy God, to provoke him to anger: I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed. And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.*

This prohibition against Idolatry was not only to Israel. The nations being driven out before them had fallen to Idolatry, forgotten the Lord God that brought them out of Noah and his sons. They committed abominations. They behaved as **Romans 1**:18-**25** describes; reprobate.

*For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness; Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them. For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened. Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools, And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things. Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.*

Moses tells them that they will suffer the same judgment as a nation if they turn to idols. That they will be destroyed, made desolate, driven from their homeland, scattered. This is God's judgment on all nations that turn from Him to serve idols, and even moreso those nations claiming to be called His.

This same judgment that destroyed the Canaanites, ultimately destroyed the Israelites, who were rejected of God. Reprobate silver. Given up and given over to their vain imaginations. And this same judgment exists today.

Roman Catholicism and Orthodoxy especially, have turned entire nations to idolatry, and in doing so, brought the judgment of God upon them. This is why Europe was overrun with Muslims in the past, and why it is happening again today. And in other Christian nations that have allowed altars to idols to flourish are seeing the same judgment, especially America.

More than Sodomites, more than antichrist Jews, people claiming to be Christian yet bowing and praying to idols, worshiping the created more than the Creator, are the reason for our current state.

We are overrun with the fruits of a Reprobate mind; sodomy and abominations. We are being ethnically cleansed. Our children barren and filled with all unrighteousness. And it first starts with idolatry. This is the primary lesson of the Reprobate Doctrine.

teachings.title: Seek the Lord while he may be found
teachings.summary: God is longsuffering, but there comes a point when He withdraws Himself from a nation or an individual and they become reprobate, so men must seek Him now while He may be found.
teachings.text:
The Lord is not happy with Israel. The priests and kings having led the people to ruin. Ephraim, Judah, Benjamin, all get named along with greater Israel for their condemnation.

Is there any judgment upon a nation as fearsome as their seeking the Lord and not being able to find Him, because He has withdrawn Himself from them?

**Jeremiah 6:30**
*Reprobate silver shall men call them, because the Lord hath rejected them*.

God is long-suffering, He is mercy that He will repent of evil He would do to a people if they turn from their wicked ways, and seek His face. But at some point, He will withdraw the offer, and allow His wrath to pour out on the wicked.

This is the same for individuals. Reprobation is real. The hour of salvation is here, now. Don't put it off. Seek Him while He can be found.

**Isaiah 55:6-7**
*Seek ye the Lord while he may be found, call ye upon him while he is near: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the unrighteous man his thoughts: and let him return unto the Lord, and he will have mercy upon him; and to our God, for he will abundantly pardon.*

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.*

**Matthew 13:14-15**
*And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.*

teachings.title: The Lord hath made all things for himself
teachings.summary: God judges the spirit behind men's deeds and uses even the wicked, like Assyria, for His purposes, so we should commit our works to Him and walk in the fear of the Lord, which brings wisdom and makes even our enemies be at peace with us.
teachings.text:
Following the opening verse, we get a quick succession of proverbs that highlight the way of the Lord, and insight to His understanding.

The Lord judges the ways of a man by the spirit behind what we do. Men may justify every deed and word, but it is the intent and heart behind them that God cares about. A man can do good for bad reasons, he can do evil with good intentions. We do things in ignorance, we do things willfully, and so God judges righteous judgement, as only He can.

And so, to ensure we are walking in His ways, we are encouraged to commit our works to the Lord and our thoughts will be established. The spirit behind our deeds will be His, rather than our vain rationalizations.

The Lord has made all creation, everything that is, is His. Even the wicked who do evil serve a purpose for the Lord. Consider Assyria;

**Isaiah 10:1-6**
*Woe unto them that decree unrighteous decrees, and that write grievousness which they have prescribed; To turn aside the needy from judgment, and to take away the right from the poor of my people, that widows may be their prey, and that they may rob the fatherless! And what will ye do in the day of visitation, and in the desolation which shall come from far? to whom will ye flee for help? and where will ye leave your glory? Without me they shall bow down under the prisoners, and they shall fall under the slain. For all this his anger is not turned away, but his hand is stretched out still. O Assyrian, the rod of mine anger, and the staff in their hand is mine indignation. I will send him against an hypocritical nation, and against the people of my wrath will I give him a charge, to take the spoil, and to take the prey, and to tread them down like the mire of the streets.*

The destruction of the northern kingdom of Israel by the heathen empire was done by the wicked. Assyria is described as the rod of God's anger. Again the sovereignty and judgment of the Lord results in all things being for His purpose. Not determinism, but utility of the ultimate authority, towards His ends.

The proud of heart are an abomination to the Lord, even when they join forces against Him. I think of the armies Satan deceives into attacking Jesus and the camp of the saints at the end of the Millennial Kingdom, appealing to their pride. They unite for the battle of Gog and Magog, and are instantly destroyed, punished for their pride.

**Revelation 20:7-9**
*And when the thousand years are expired, Satan shall be loosed out of his prison, And shall go out to deceive the nations which are in the four quarters of the earth, Gog, and Magog, to gather them together to battle: the number of whom is as the sand of the sea. And they went up on the breadth of the earth, and compassed the camp of the saints about, and the beloved city: and fire came down from God out of heaven, and devoured them.*

As we have been instructed over and over again, fear of the Lord brings understanding and wisdom, wisdom brings mercy and love of truth, and these in practice purge iniquity and injustice from men.

By heeding the wisdom of the Lord, by seeking and walking in His paths, by acknowledging Him in all our ways, we please the Lord and rather than the destruction of the prideful and the visiting of evil, He will even make our enemies be at peace with us.

In **Genesis 26:28-29**, Isaac prospered and lived righteously, causing his chief enemy, King Abimelech, to come to him seeking a covenant of peace, acknowledging that God was with him.

This is most evident in the cycle of Judges.

**Judges 2:14-19**
*And the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he delivered them into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them, and he sold them into the hands of their enemies round about, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies. Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them: and they were greatly distressed. Nevertheless the Lord raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them.*

teachings.title: The Lord pondereth the hearts
teachings.summary: God ordains rulers and directs the king's heart, and He judges the spirit behind men's deeds, valuing mercy and judgment over sacrifice, so the sacrifice of the wicked is abomination.
teachings.text:
**Proverbs 21** adds to the sayings of the king, first hand advice of Solomon to his heir, that God is the master and commander of the ship of state, as He sets the heart of the king to His own devices.

Just as the Lord said of Pharaoh;

**Romans 9:17**
*For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up, that I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth.*

And the government is on the shoulders of whom its given;

**Romans 13:1**
*Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers. For there is no power but of God: the powers that be are ordained of God.*

What a humbling saying for a young prince to hear. For good or ill, God's anointed is ordained to power in His will and to the Almighty Lord's purpose.

*Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.* The spirit behind what a man does, this is what God judges. The things we do in sin aren't only those things that no good led to, fornication, iniquity, theft, deceit, covetousness...those aren't the only ways we sin and fall short. Often we can do the right things for the wrong reasons. God knows our hearts.

That's why, especially for a prince, to do justice and judgment, with fairness and right spirit, means more to God than sacrifice. As Jesus says to the Pharisees;

**Matthew 9:13**
*But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance*.

This, quoting **Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

This leads to a theme of the heart of the wicked. Their tendencies and traits.

The high look and proud heart of the wicked, their plans and schemes, this is sin. Diligence has a reward, haste leads to want.

Lying for wealth is a vanity, the wise king says, and it is passed back and forth between thieves, those that seek death and not life. There is no honor among thieves. Their robberies end in death. They are destroyed by their ways. They refuse judgment. Everything they seek to gain is motivated by greed and covetousness. Their way is froward and strange. But for the pure, those seeking to walk on God's path, their work is right.

The wicked desires evil. They do not love even their neighbors, violating even the second great command.

**Matthew 22:37-39**
*Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.*

In the end, God will overthrow the wicked for their wickedness. The wicked ignore the cries of the poor, and so God will not hear the wicked's cry.

Their love of pleasure results in poverty, that lack of impulse control. High time preference. This will ruin a man led by his own desires. A foolish man spends all he has.

Scorners are proud and haughty, their wrath comes from their pride. Overreacting to slights. Their pride insulted.

The lazy are their own destruction, the slothful kills themselves by their lack of labor. Their end is hunger. They shall always want.

The covetous, often the same foolish, lazy, proud and unjust fool, the robber, he who hates his neighbor, they are consumed by their greed all day long.

God promises the false witness will perish, and the wicked is set in their ways.

Tying this thread all back together to the beginning, we are given the understanding God judges hearts, the spirit of the man, and He values mercy and judgement over sacrifice, we see then the truth; *The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination: how much more, when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?*

teachings.title: Why do the heathen rage
teachings.summary: Psalm 2 prophesies the rulers' vain rebellion against God's anointed, whom God raised up and set as King over the nations, warning rulers to kiss the Son and trust in Him.
teachings.text:
Why do the heathen rage? Why do people think they can go against God? Kings and rulers, presidents and prime ministers, popes and priests, all seek to be freed from the ways of the Lord, to do what they will.

Especially the religious and political leaders in the time of Jesus.

**Acts 4:27**
*For of a truth against thy holy child Jesus, whom thou hast anointed, both Herod, and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, and the people of Israel, were gathered together*.

They believed if they killed the Son, they would break the bands, Their bonds, and be free of God.

Jesus addressed this in a parable, about a Lord who planted a vineyard and lent it out to husbandmen to dress and keep it. And when the Lord sent servants to gather the harvest, the stewards beat and killed them. So finally, the Lord sends his son;

**Matthew 21:38**
*But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance*.

David prophetically writes of this here in **Psalm 2**.

But, it is folly. The Lord holds them in derision. He laughs at their vain efforts, because Christ, His anointed, rose again.

He set His Son upon Zion, and upon the throne.

**Acts 13:32–33**
*And we declare unto you glad tidings, how that the promise which was made unto the fathers, God hath fulfilled the same unto us their children, in that he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee.*

Jesus' inheritance are all the nations of the world, and possession of the uttermost parts of the world. And as Lord of lords and King of kings, He will rule them.

**Revelation 2:26–27**
*And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.*

This prophetic Psalm gives warning to the rulers of this world, reminding them of their place. That they serve at the pleasure of the Lord, and He will deliver vengeance.

It's an amazing and consistent message, across the entire Bible; The Christ is God's anointed, and Jesus is the Christ. All who believe on Christ Jesus shall be saved. His grace and mercy giving us the chance to serve Him in righteousness.

*Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son, lest he be angry, and ye perish from the way, when his wrath is kindled but a little. Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.*

Amen
